text:
harry: quick design sync — dropped two new variants in Figma for the model compare table: "sticky-legend" (legend pinned to top + compact rows) and "split-badges" (primary badge inline, secondary collapsed). GIF: https://imgur.com/mock-compare. Need takes on discoverability, keyboard flow, and pin wording.

morgan: first impression: sticky legend helps when you scroll horizontally and you lose context of badge colors. Compact rows look good but metric alignment must be fixed so columns don't jump when numbers change.

leah: accessibility: the sticky legend must be reachable by keyboard and announced to screen readers when it appears. Suggest a skip-link "Skip to legend" and `role=region` with `aria-label="Performance legend"`. Also, do not rely on hover-only tooltips for thresholds.

harry: good call. For the collapsed secondary badges I prototyped a small "•+2" button. Click opens a lightweight panel with full metrics. Is `role=dialog` for that panel ok or should it be `menu`?

leah: use `role=dialog` with `aria-modal=false` since it's informational. Ensure focus is moved into the dialog and Esc closes it. Use `aria-label="More metrics for model X"`. Also add textual thresholds in the dialog (not only color).

morgan: about pin scope — engineering prefers workspace scope by default. UX question: how obvious should scope be? I proposed a tiny org glyph next to the pin when it's workspace-scoped and a tooltip that reads "Pinned to workspace".

harry: that resonates. What about microcopy for the pin control? Options I sketched: 
  A) "Pin version to compare"
  B) "Pin for quick-compare"
  C) "Add to compare set"
Which do people prefer?

leah: A is clearest for SR users. For the visible label keep it short (Pin). For screen readers use explicit states: `aria-label="Pin model v1.2 to compare"` and when toggled `aria-label="Unpin model v1.2 from compare (pinned to workspace)"` plus `aria-pressed` change.

morgan: also, when multiple pins exist the filter bar should show a removable chip like "Pinned (3)" so users realize the compare set changed. That chip needs `aria-label="Remove pinned versions filter (3)"` and keyboard deletion support.

harry: agreed. Small interaction question: should pinning auto-open the compare flyout or just update the chip? My leaning: only update chip and show a short non-modal toast "Pinned to workspace" (1.6s).

devops: backend note: pins are stored with a scope field already, but we'll need UI flag to render the org glyph. Also recommend debounce on pin API to avoid duplicate requests when someone taps quickly.

leah: badges: do not rely on color-only. Add iconography (clock for latency, bolt for throughput, dollar for cost) and include text shortcuts in collapsed view, e.g., "L: 120ms". Legend should include thresholds, e.g., "Latency: <120ms (good), 12050ms (warn), >250ms (bad)" — these are examples, validate numbers with SRE.

morgan: focus style — in compact rows the 3px blue halo feels heavy. Propose 2px solid focus + 3px inner padding to avoid clipping badges. Run contrast checks against tile background.

harry: added that to the figma notes. QA: can you run a quick keyboard-only pass and a NVDA/VoiceOver spot check?

qa-bot: Automated checklist: 1) legend skip-link present, 2) more-metrics dialog traps focus and Esc closes, 3) pin toggle uses `aria-pressed` and SR labels, 4) pinned-chip keyboard-removable, 5) badges have icon + text, 6) focus outline = 2px solid in compact mode. Marking as pending manual verification.

leah: one more a11y nit — avoid hover-only expansions (like showing metric labels on hover). Ensure expand-on-focus works and that all hover reveals are keyboard-available.

morgan: tiny UX nit on copy for the toast after pin: prefer "Pinned to workspace" over "Pinned to compare" since it's clearer about scope. Keep it short.

harry: ok final checklist for PR: sticky legend implementation + skip-link, collapsed-badges dialog semantics, pin toggle SR copy + org glyph, pinned-chip filter behavior, focus style tweak, and update toasts. I'll push a branch and tag @leah @morgan for final sign-off. React with :thumbsup: for go-ahead, :eyes: for more changes. Thanks!
